title.en: Symmetry composition table, closure and noncommutativity

summary: Verify the composition table of a finite symmetry set, its defining relations and a noncommuting pair, using exact permutations.
objective: The table is closed with inverses present, the defining relations hold exactly, and order-dependent outcomes differ visibly.
applies_when: A scene applies rotations and reflections to a labelled figure.
Operations can be composed in a chosen order.
Animation displays a transition between two discrete configurations.
intent_signals: does the order of these two symmetries matter
check that the symmetry set is closed
example_prompts: Check the composition rules of the square symmetry scene.

principles: Symmetry operations are elements of a finite group, so the check belongs on the composition table rather than on the animation that displays a transition. Closure, inverses and associativity are general; the specific relations checked below belong to the square fixture, since other finite symmetry groups are abelian or have different orders.
Order matters: a noncommuting pair must give two different labelled outcomes, which is the observable distinguishing a group action from a picture.

Labels are tracking markers on an unlabelled shape: they let you tell two outcomes apart without changing which motions map the shape to itself. If instead the labels themselves must be preserved, the figure has fewer symmetries, and the record says which of the two the scene means.
implementation: Represent each operation as a permutation of the labelled corners and build the full composition table by composing permutations.
Verify closure by checking that every product appears in the element list, and verify that every element has an inverse in the list.

For the square fixture, check the defining relations directly: the quarter turn to the fourth power, the reflection squared, and the reflection conjugating the rotation to its inverse. For a different figure, check the relations its own presentation declares.
Confirm that every operation preserves the figure by comparing all pairwise corner distances before and after.
observable_checks: The composition table is closed and every row and column is a permutation of the element list; a missing or repeated entry identifies a wrong permutation.
The declared relations for this figure hold exactly as permutations with no floating-point comparison, and committing an animated transition reproduces the same permutation.

For the square fixture the chosen noncommuting pair produces two different corner labelings in the two orders, and pairwise corner distances are unchanged by every operation; on an abelian figure the noncommutativity case is reported as inapplicable instead of failing.

known_limits: Covers the declared plane figure and its labelled vertices; the rotation group of a three-dimensional solid is a different subject.
Authored verification guidance; no computation or render was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: The symmetries of the square form a dihedral group of eight elements generated by a quarter turn r and a reflection s, with r to the fourth equal to the identity, s squared equal to the identity, and s r s equal to r inverse.
claims.scope: The dihedral group of the square presented in the cited text as vertex permutations; naming conventions for this group differ between texts.
